title: qmd feed --source SYSTEM (--after TOKEN | --since-arrival ISO) [--limit N] --json
description: What is new to me: every document version qmd wrote for one source system, in arrival order, resumable by an opaque token. Use this, not time windows, to enumerate; an item published late with an old item time still appears here. Times are epoch seconds (UTC). QMD_UNTIL applies as it does to every read.
x-invariants: Tokens are totally ordered within a source and are never reused.
No gap: once a token T has been returned, qmd never writes a new version for that source at a position at or before T.
At least once: a version may be returned again after a restart; consumers dedupe on (id, version).

--since-arrival T is exact for T at or after the arrival epoch (the first deploy of qmd.feed.v1; versions written earlier carry arrived null): it starts at the first version whose arrival is at or after T. A T before the epoch exits 2 naming the epoch; it never silently starts late.
--after and --since-arrival are mutually exclusive; giving neither is a usage error (exit 2): a consumer always chooses its start.
Under QMD_UNTIL, head is the newest position visible under the ceiling, so complete stays reachable for a replaying consumer.

source.description: One source system, never a group.

token.description: Position of this version; pass as --after to continue after it.

id.description: Native doc id (K1); fetch the document with qmd get.

item.description: The search-result unit this doc belongs to (K1).

time.description: The item's own time at the source.

arrived.description: When qmd wrote this version; null for versions written before the arrival epoch (the first deploy of qmd.feed.v1).

from.description: Sender address or number as qmd renders it.

thread.description: Provider thread id (Gmail thread); null where the source has none.

chat.description: Canonical WhatsApp chat (phone-number JID); null for other sources.

version.description: The K2 version of this doc; (id, version) identifies one returned row.

reparse.description: Written by a reparse of existing raw records, not by a new capture; content may be unchanged.

next.description: Token to pass as --after next time: the last returned item's token, or the start position when nothing was returned.

head.description: The newest position for this source visible to the caller (under QMD_UNTIL when set) at read time; null if none.

complete.description: next == head: the consumer has seen everything written so far.
